newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed but Frankfurt hits record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed but Frankfurt hits record.

text.p: European bourses, rattled by an unsteady performance on Wall Street, were mixed on Wednesday after setting a record-breaking pace earlier this week.
The dollar edged higher in quiet dealings, buoyed by news of hefty Japanese capital outflows into foreign investments, which would help the dollar against the yen.
German stocks were the stars, climbing to a record close of 2702.99 points on the DAX index largely on the strength of a buoyant telecoms sector.
Frankfurt's performance, shruging off a poor overnight showing by Wall Street, eclipsed its earlier closing peak set only two days ago of 2702.64.
Telecoms sector was the main focus after utility group RWE AG revealed a surprise shift in allegiances, boosting its stocks and those of its prospective German partner Veba AG.
"Telecoms are certainly the big news today," said a Frankfurt dealer.
But other European bourses fell, depressed in early trading by Wall Street's negative close and later by its poor opening with profit-takers moving after recent gains.

They were pausing for breath after a bull-run that has drawn strength from signs that the U.S. economy, which has grown rapidly, was slowing to a level of inflation-free growth and low interest rates.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped by 0.4 percent after closing at a high of 4035.6 points on the FTSE index on Tuesday, its fourth consecutive closing record largely fuelled by Wall Street's surge.

London fell by 16.2 points to 4019.4. "We've had some heavyweights suffering badly today -- drugs, Glaxo, ICI and British Telecom -- and that brought the index down. But the market feels well underpinned and it would take a major crack on Wall Street to drag it down," one trader said.
"We've had a terrific run and if you take out the big losers today, the market has been fine," he added.

London markets were little affected by the minutes of the last monetary meeting between finance minister Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George, which confirmed George had pressed for higher rates to ward off inflationary dangers.

Paris shares slipped in and out of positive territory but traders said a firm tone to the franc and to bonds was seen lending support to the market. The CAC index was down slightly at 6.44 points at 2155.10 by mid-afternoon.
"If the CAC 40 is able to break through the 2,165 level then we could end up with a good rise at the end of the day," said one dealer.
The dollar strengthened slightly against the yen and the mark, supported by the Japanese capital outflows data and the fact the mark was weaker against other European currencies.
But with little direction before Friday's data on U.S. September producer prices and retail sales, dealers said they expected little movement at all in the short term.
"The next event is the U.S. data. I see the market remaining quite dull until then. The trend is in place," said Paul Lambert, senior economist at UBS in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5290 marks and 111.52 yen compared with 1.5268 marks and 111.22 yen late in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 16.2 points at 4019.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 6.44 at 2,155.10.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed at 2702.99, up 11.82.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $381.35 in the afternoon, compared with Tuesday's close of $381.00. Silver was indicated at $4.94, compared to $4.90.
